findings.finding: the delimiter choice preferred the widest header over a consistent one; Name;Area, sq m, gross;Id was read as comma
findings.fix: TS chooseTableDelimiter and Python choose_delimiter: among candidates with more than one field and the same count on every sampled line, the largest count wins; candidate order breaks ties; comma only when none is consistent
tests: delimited-text.test.ts: a consistent delimiter wins over a wider but inconsistent header

findings.finding: a small GeoJSON kept through /uploads needed the processor inside the case lock; a processor 503 or timeout rolled back enrolment
findings.fix: prepareRetainedGeojsonTx turns any processor failure other than its 413/422 refusals into BOUNDED_READER_UNAVAILABLE; retainedGeojsonAdapterTx then takes the pre-RT1 streaming route and writes the reason, naming only the failure code, on the item; a source that already has an intake-large job stays streamed, so a later enrolment never starts a second reader
findings.test: intake-large-steps.test.ts: a small kept GeoJSON whose processor is unavailable is enrolled on the streaming reader, with the reason
findings.movedBeforeLockReason: queueIntakeDraftTx is reached from five transactional callers (intake-service publish, intake-draft-worker approval, three service.ts paths); moving the whole read and inspect-gis out would mean computing it ahead in each caller, threading it through queueIntakeSurfaceTx/queueIntakeDraftTx and revalidating it against the source pin, which is not a small change. A failing processor no longer fails enrolment, but a slow one can still hold the case lock up to the 60 s processor timeout.
findings.reasonLifetime: the reason is the item's limit_reason until the streaming reader's first projection replaces it; the outbox event of that write keeps it
